NI003 instructs the Certification Body on the audit of the product developer's operational processes that maintain the security of the certified wallet: version control, change management, update delivery and vulnerability management. [NP001] section 6.1 (phase 4) refers to it as the audit instruction, and section 7 lists it as the instruction for the audit of developer operational processes. Criteria marked [proposed] are drafting proposals of this document, derived from the sources named, and are not yet decided.

| Version   | Date            | Summary of change               |
|-----------|-----------------|---------------------------------|
| RC1.0     | 24 October 2026 | Aligned to [NP001] and [NP002]. |

## 1 Introduction {#s-1}

### 1.1 Purpose {#s-1-1}

A certificate of conformity says something about one version of the wallet. The product developer keeps the wallet secure afterwards through its operational processes. [NP001] section 2.2 therefore scopes the management system element of the scheme to the processes directly relevant to the security maintenance of the certified product, and states that general information security management systems are not part of the certification decision. This instruction states what the CB audits in those processes, how, and how findings feed the certificate.

### 1.2 Scope {#s-1-2}

- The four processes of section 4: version control, change management, update delivery, and vulnerability management. Annex IX of [IR 2981] names version control, update and vulnerability management; [NP001] section 2.2 names change management, vulnerability management and update delivery. This instruction covers all of them [see the review point below].
- The continued validity of the functional certificate and of the assumptions and certificates the certification relies on (section 4.5).
- The initial audit (design and existence of the processes, not yet operating effectiveness), the annual surveillance audits (operating effectiveness) and the audit within recertification.

Out of scope: general information security management, software development lifecycle assurance, conformity with the Cyber Resilience Act as a whole ([NP001] section 2.2), and the evaluation tasks of [NI002].

### 1.3 Involved roles {#s-1-3}

| Role              | Entity                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|-------------------|-----------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Lead auditor      | Certification Body    | Plans and leads the audit, decides on the findings, signs the audit report. Competent per section 6.                                                                                             |
| Auditor           | Certification Body    | Performs audit activities under the lead auditor.                                                                                                                                                |
| Auditee           | Product developer     | Provides the process documentation and the records, and makes the process owners available.                                                                                                      |
| Technical support | Evaluation Laboratory | May support the CB with technical questions on the evidence, under the CB's responsibility. [Proposed; [NP001] section 3.2 assigns the audit to the CB and does not mention laboratory support.] |

### 1.4 Conventions {#s-1-4}

"Shall" marks a requirement taken from [NP001], [NP002], [IR 2981] or [EN 17640], with the source named. Criteria marked [proposed] are drafting proposals. Epistemic tags follow [NP001].

## 2 Audit principles {#s-2}

The audit is evidence based. The auditor shall verify statements by records and, where the audit type requires it, by observation or interview; a process description alone does not demonstrate operating effectiveness. The audit is performed by persons independent of the process audited and of the evaluation, in line with the impartiality required of the CB by [ISO/IEC 17065]. [ISO 19011] (guidelines for auditing management systems) is a useful informative reference for audit practice; this instruction does not make it normative [inferred suitability, not checked against the standard text].

Confidential information of the product developer obtained during the audit is protected under the CB's accreditation obligations. Source code and vulnerability details are shown to the auditor only as far as needed to verify the process.

## 3 Audit types and schedule {#s-3}

The schedule follows the reference schedule of Annex IX of [IR 2981] and [NP002] section 7.1. The Regulation makes the schedule a recommendation; any other schedule must keep the certificate validity within five years and each evaluation within 12 months of the previous year's.

| Year    | Audit type                                   | Auditor verifies                                                                                                                                                                                          | Audit stages                                                          |
|---------|----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 0       | Initial audit ([NP001] section 6.1, phase 4) | That the four processes exist and are designed to meet the criteria of section 4. Operating effectiveness is not assessed [Annex IX: maintenance processes excluding their operating effectiveness].      | Document review; walk-through with process owners.                   |
| 1, 2, 3 | Surveillance audit                           | Operating effectiveness of at least version control, update and vulnerability management; evaluation of changes impacting the security of the product, using the delta assessment of [NP001] section 6.6. | Document review; record sampling; interviews.                         |
| 4       | Audit within recertification                 | Operating effectiveness of the maintenance processes, with the criteria applied to the whole period since the last full evaluation.                                                                       | As surveillance, plus reconsideration of the design of the processes. |
| Any     | Special audit                                | Triggered under [NP002] section 7.3, for instance after a vulnerability, a suspension or a change concluded as not covered. Scope set by the CB.                                                          | As the CB determines.                                                 |

## 4 Audit criteria {#s-4}

The criteria below are what the processes shall achieve. Each has an identifier, used in the audit report and in Annex A. Evidence examples are indicative.

### 4.1 Version control (VC) {#s-4-1}

| ID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Criterion                                         | Source   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------|----------|
| Every release of the certified Wallet Instance is uniquely identified by application identifier, version name, version code and build or release identifier, and these match the identifiers on the functional certificate and in the FIT ST. | [NP001] 6.2, 6.2.1                                | VC1      |
| The source code and build configuration of every release are held under version control with traceable history and controlled access, so that the delivered package can be related to a source revision.                                      | [proposed]; supports [NP001] Annex C items 1 to 5 | VC2      |
| The signing key and the signing process are controlled, and a change of the signing key is notified to the CB before it is used.                                                                                                              | [NP001] 6.6 (signing key change)                  | VC3      |
| The list of third-party components, libraries and SDKs per release is maintained.                                                                                                                                                             | [proposed]; [NP001] Annex C item 6                | VC4      |

### 4.2 Change management (CM) {#s-4-2}

| ID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Criterion                     | Source   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------|----------|
| Planned changes to the certified product are notified to the CB before implementation.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | [NP001] 3.4; [NP002] 7.4      | CM1      |
| Every change is recorded with a description of all differences, not only those the developer considers security relevant, so that a delta assessment is possible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          | [NP001] Annex C item 4        | CM2      |
| Each change is assessed for security impact, including against the list of changes in [NP001] section 6.6 that shall not be concluded as covered without new analysis: the user authentication protocol or factors, the interface with the WSCA-BE or WSCD, key handling, attestation handling, resilience mechanisms, trusted list and revocation handling, target platform API level, signing key, distribution channel. | [NP001] 6.6                   | CM3      |
| Changes to the TOE boundary, to the assumptions on the operational environment, to the environmental requirements or to the identity or version of a certified component are identified as such and are not treated as covered by delta assessment.                                                                                                                                                                        | [NP001] 6.6                   | CM4      |
| Changes to the target platform and to the variants for categories of end user devices are tracked, because wallet instances are expected to need frequent updates.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | [IR 2981] Annex IV, section 5 | CM5      |

### 4.3 Update delivery (UD) {#s-4-3}

| ID   | Criterion                                                                                                                               | Source             |
|------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|
| UD1  | The product has a feature to perform updates of each software component, and the update process is described and operated as described. | [IR 2981] Annex IX |
| Updates are produced from controlled builds, signed with the controlled key, and the integrity and authenticity of an update is verified before installation.                                               | [proposed]                                 | UD2      |
| The distribution channel is the one stated in the FIT ST and any change of channel is notified ([NP001] section 6.6).                                                                                       | [NP001] 6.6                                | UD3      |
| The time between availability of a security update and its delivery to users, and the share of users on supported versions, are monitored.                                                                  | [proposed]                                 | UD4      |
| The Wallet Instance's mechanism for verifying, per wallet unit, that the platform satisfies the assumptions on the end user device remains effective after updates, including the minimum platform version. | [IR 2981] Annex IV, section 4; [NP001] 2.4 | UD5      |

### 4.4 Vulnerability management (VM) {#s-4-4}

| ID                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | Criterion                                   | Source   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|----------|
| The product developer has a vulnerability management policy and procedures that take into account [ISO/IEC 30111], and that meet the requirements of Annex I to the Cyber Resilience Act as required by Article 5(7) of [IR 2981].     | [IR 2981] Art. 5(3), 5(7); [NP001] 3.4, 6.4 | VM1      |
| Sources of vulnerability information (public databases, dependency advisories, platform security bulletins, researcher reports) are monitored and the monitoring is evidenced.                                                         | [proposed]                                  | VM2      |
| Each vulnerability is assessed for severity and impact in the context of the certified wallet.                                                                                                                                         | [NP001] 6.4                                 | VM3      |
| Critical vulnerabilities and active exploits are notified to the CB within 24 hours of discovery, and high-severity vulnerabilities within 72 hours. Other vulnerabilities and changes are notified within the timeline of the scheme. | [NP001] 3.4, 6.4                            | VM4      |
| A vulnerability impact analysis report is prepared for any vulnerability that affects the software components of the wallet, with the content of Article 5(5), and transmitted to the CB without undue delay.                          | [IR 2981] Art. 5(5), 5(6)                   | VM5      |
| Remediation is carried out commensurately with severity and potential impact, with remediation delays recorded.                                                                                                                        | [IR 2981] Art. 12(3); [EN 17640] 6.9.4.5    | VM6      |
| Publicly known and remediated vulnerabilities are disclosed and registered in the repositories of Annex V.                                                                                                                             | [IR 2981] Art. 5(9)                         | VM7      |

Evidence expectations drawn from [EN 17640] 6.9.4.5, which describes the evidence from the development process for vulnerability testing: vulnerability scan reports no older than three months; a sample of remediation actions annexed to the internal vulnerability management policy with remediation delays clearly indicated; and a risk management analysis covering at least the 12 months before the evaluation, with unambiguous version tracking. For the audit they are a reference for what a mature process leaves behind [inferred use].

### 4.5 Continued validity of the certification basis (CV) {#s-4-5}

| ID                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Criterion        | Source   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------|----------|
| The functional certificate remains valid for the certified version, and its suspension, withdrawal or expiry is notified to the CB without undue delay.                                                    | [NP001] 3.4, 6.2 | CV1      |
| The product developer monitors the validity, version and certification status of the WSCD certificate and of other certificates recorded as environmental requirements, and notifies the CB of any change. | [NP001] 5.4, 6.6 | CV2      |
| The assumptions on the operational environment and the environmental requirements of the Protection Profile remain valid for the lifetime of the certificate.                                              | [NP001] 2.4      | CV3      |

## 5 Audit procedure {#s-5}

### 5.1 Planning {#s-5-1}

The lead auditor sends the product developer the audit plan with the scope, the criteria, the period to be covered, the documents and records requested, and the dates. For surveillance audits the period is the time since the last audit, and the request includes the change log, the vulnerability log, the notifications sent to the CB and the update release log for that period.

### 5.2 Document review {#s-5-2}

The auditor reviews the process documentation against the criteria and records for each criterion whether the design meets it. In the initial audit this is the principal activity.

### 5.3 Sampling of records {#s-5-3}

For operating effectiveness the auditor samples records of the period. [Proposed] sampling rule: all changes that the product developer or the CB classified as touching the list of [NP001] section 6.6; all vulnerabilities rated critical or high; all notifications to the CB; and a sample of other changes and vulnerabilities selected by the auditor, with the sampling basis stated in the report. The auditor traces each sampled change from request to release and to the next delta assessment, and each sampled vulnerability from discovery to notification, remediation and disclosure, checking the 24 and 72 hour limits against timestamps.

### 5.4 Interviews and observation {#s-5-4}

The auditor interviews the owners of the four processes and, where useful, observes a build or update release. The aim is to see that the people who operate the process know it and follow it.

### 5.5 Findings {#s-5-5}

The auditor records for each criterion: met, not met, or not applicable with the reason. [Proposed] classification of a not-met criterion:

| Class                                                                                                                                                                                     | Meaning                                                                                                                               | Consequence           |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|
| A criterion is not met in conformity in doubt, for example a missed 24 or 72 hour notification, a change that required a delta assessment and had none, or a process that does not exist. | continued Reported to the certifying function; may lead to suspension under [NP002] section 9.2. Remediation timeframe set by the CB. | Major a way that puts |
| A criterion is partly met, or a record is missing, without putting conformity in doubt.                                                                                                   | Corrective action by a date set by the CB; verified at the next audit.                                                                | Minor                 |
| An improvement that does not concern a criterion.                                                                                                                                         | Recorded; no action required.                                                                                                         | Observation           |

### 5.6 Audit report {#s-5-6}

The CB issues an audit report to the product developer with the scope, the period, the criteria, the evidence examined, the sampling basis, the findings with their class, and the conclusion. A recommended outline is in Annex B. The report is an input to the certification decision ([NP002] section 6.1) in the initial audit, and to the surveillance report ([NP002] section 7.2) later. The CB keeps the records for the period set by the Scheme Owner ([NP001] section 3.2).

## 6 Auditor competence {#s-6}

The auditor shall have the competence required by [ISO/IEC 17065] for certification personnel, knowledge of the wallet and its threat model, and knowledge of secure software maintenance and vulnerability handling for mobile applications ([NP001] section 3.2).

## Annex A: Audit checklist {#s-a}

One row per criterion. The columns for the initial audit and the surveillance audit say what the auditor looks for.

| ID                                         | Criterion (short)                                    | Initial audit: look for                                                              | Surveillance audit: look for   |
|--------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| Release identifiers                        | Process description of release identification        | Release log against functional certificate and FIT ST for each release in the period | VC1                            |
| Source and build control                   | Repository and access control description            | Sample trace from delivered package to source revision                               | VC2                            |
| Signing key control                        | Key management description                           | Records of key use; any key change and its notification                              | VC3                            |
| Third-party components                     | Component inventory process                          | Inventory per release; changes since last audit                                      | VC4                            |
| Notification before implementation         | Change notification procedure                        | Notifications against release log                                                    | CM1                            |
| Complete change description                | Change record template                               | Sampled change records against source differences                                    | CM2                            |
| Security impact assessment                 | Assessment procedure and list of [NP001] 6.6 changes | Sampled assessments; changes of the listed kinds and their delta assessments         | CM3                            |
| Boundary and environment changes           | Procedure to identify them                           | Any such change in the period and how it was treated                                 | CM4                            |
| Platform and variant tracking              | Procedure                                            | Platform and API level changes in the period                                         | CM5                            |
| Update feature per component               | Update mechanism description                         | Update release log; evidence of updates delivered                                    | UD1                            |
| Signed, verified updates                   | Release and verification description                 | Sampled release signing records                                                      | UD2                            |
| Distribution channel                       | Channel description                                  | Evidence of channel for each release                                                 | UD3                            |
| Update timeliness                          | Monitoring approach                                  | Time from fix availability to delivery for sampled security updates                  | UD4                            |
| Platform assumption verification           | Description of the mechanism                         | Evidence it was retained and functional after updates                                | UD5                            |
| Policy per [ISO/IEC 30111] and CRA Annex I | The policy and procedures                            | Policy review dates; operation as described                                          | VM1                            |
| Monitoring of sources                      | Source list and method                               | Monitoring records for the period                                                    | VM2                            |
| Severity and impact assessment             | Method                                               | Sampled assessments                                                                  | VM3                            |
| 24 and 72 hour notification                | Notification procedure and contacts                  | Timestamps of discovery and notification for sampled vulnerabilities                 | VM4                            |
| VIAR                                     | Template and procedure            | VIARs of the period; transmission date                                 | VM5                            |
| Remediation commensurate with severity   | Remediation targets               | Remediation delays recorded for sampled vulnerabilities                | VM6                            |
| Disclosure in Annex V repositories       | Disclosure procedure              | Registrations in the period                                            | VM7                            |
| Functional certificate validity          | Monitoring approach               | Current status; any change and its notification                        | CV1                            |
| Certificates of environmental components | Monitoring approach               | Status of WSCD and other certificates; any change and its notification | CV2                            |
| Assumptions remain valid                 | Monitoring approach [placeholder] | As the Protection Profile states                                       | CV3                            |

## Annex B: Audit report outline [proposed] {#s-b}

|   # | Section               | Content                                                                                                                          |
|-----|-----------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
|   1 | Identification        | Product, version, certificate identifier, CB, product developer, audit type, period covered, dates, auditors.                    |
|   2 | Scope and criteria    | Processes and criteria identifiers audited; exclusions with reasons.                                                             |
|   3 | Evidence and sampling | Documents and records examined, sampling basis, interviews held.                                                                 |
|   4 | Results per criterion | Met, not met (class), or not applicable with reason.                                                                             |
|   5 | Changes in the period | Changes examined and the delta conclusions reached or required.                                                                  |
|   6 | Conclusion            | Whether the processes meet the criteria; recommended actions; input to the certification decision or to the surveillance report. |
